findings.body:
`_read_github_event_repo_visibility()` only reads `repository.visibility`. When that field is missing/empty it returns `unknown`, and both the write-tier override and private fail-open require `private|internal` — so `unknown` behaves like public and the under-report fix never fires.

GitHub event payloads have long included the boolean `repository.private`, and Actions also exposes `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_VISIBILITY`. Prefer `visibility`, then fall back to `private: true/false`, then the env var, before `unknown`. Add a unit test for the fallback path.

`main()` calls `gh_get_collaborator_permission` whenever the webhook association misses the allow-list, with no visibility guard. On public repos the enhanced resolver never lets permission override the association, so this is a wasted REST round-trip on every external PR — and it contradicts `docs/SECURITY.md`, which says the lookup happens only on private/internal when the webhook mismatches.

Gate the call with `_is_private_or_internal_visibility(repo_visibility)` (after fixing the visibility reader above). Public denies stay association-only and keep the zero-API cheapest-first property.

This example still says empty `author-association` is “only sensible for private repos,” but the rest of the PR (SECURITY/README/setup) now recommends keeping the default on private repos and using `''` only to fully disable the gate. Worth a one-line doc sync so copy-paste consumers don’t reintroduce the old workaround.

summary:
## Verdict

Solid fix for the private-org webhook under-report, with good docs/tests coverage — two gate-path warnings should land before merge so the permission fallback actually fires and stays cheapest-first on public repos.

## Narrative

The core design is right: keep public repos association-only, allow `admin`/`maintain`/`write` to override a weak webhook association only on private/internal, fail-open there and fail-closed on public, and emit an actionable log line. `resolve_author_association_gate_enhanced` matches that contract, and the pure-logic tests cover the main matrix (private admin/write allow, private none deny, public no override, empty gate, fail-open/closed, internal).

Two implementation gaps undercut the private-repo fix and the documented cost model:

1. **Visibility detection is brittle.** `_read_github_event_repo_visibility()` only reads `repository.visibility`. If that field is absent, visibility becomes `unknown`, which is treated like public — so neither the permission override nor private fail-open runs. Prefer `visibility`, then `repository.private`, then `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_VISIBILITY`.
2. **Permission lookup is not visibility-gated in `main()`.** Every allow-list miss (including public external PRs) hits the collaborators/permission API even though the enhanced resolver never uses the result on public repos. That contradicts `docs/SECURITY.md` (“one GitHub permission lookup on private/internal…”) and weakens the cheapest-first abuse gate.

Also worth a small doc sync: `examples/open-source-safe.yml` still frames `author-association: ''` as the private-repo recommendation while README/SECURITY/setup now say the default is fine.

## What looks good

- No public-contract break (`author-association` semantics extended, not renamed/removed).
- Stdlib-only, typed helpers, broad `except` with `# noqa: BLE001` + WHY.
- Username path-segment quoting via `urllib.parse.quote`.
- Docs + setup skill + CHANGELOG updated in lockstep with the behavi
